messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH - dedicated-tenant-latency for tenant=acme-finance-dedicated (pool=dedicated-us-west-2-3). p95 latency > 2.5s for 3m, error rate increased. PD: PD#45678

pagerduty: page fired to rotation: oncall-engineering. Escalation policy: 10m -> sre-lead.

maria (oncall): Acked. I'm looking. 1) Which routes impacted? 2) Any autoscaler events?

sam (infra): I'm on it. checking pool metrics now. grabbing pod / node stats.

luis (sre): also seeing increased queue length on prefix-cache for ACME. could be KV eviction storm.

maria (oncall): @tenant-ops-bot get-pool-metrics dedicated-us-west-2-3 5m

tenant-ops-bot: Pool metrics (5m): cpu_util=82%, gpu_mem_util=94%, pod_restarts=0, inflight_requests=620, target_replicas=6, current_replicas=6

sam (infra): running quick checks:
```
kubectl -n dedicated-acme get pods -o wide
NAME                                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   IP           NODE
serving-0                              2/2     Running   0          12d  10.2.4.5     g4dn-12-1
serving-1                              2/2     Running   0          1h   10.2.4.6     g4dn-12-2
serving-2                              1/2     OOMKill   1          3h   10.2.4.7     g4dn-12-3
```

sam (infra): pod serving-2 got OOMKilled a few hours ago, GPU mem pressure high on node g4dn-12-3. Also noticed KV cache evictions heavily spiked.

maria (oncall): customer impact? which tenants behind that pool?

jess (cs): ACME Finance (acme-finance-dedicated) is on that pool; they reported timeouts on a few endpoints. I DM'd them that we're investigating.

luis (sre): logs show lots of large-context requests with long sequence lengths for ACME. prefix cache thrash: many cache misses -> regen -> memory blowup.

maria (oncall): quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily route ACME traffic to hosted fallback model (lower perf but stable), 2) scale up the dedicated pool by 2 GPUs, 3) apply request throttling for very large seqs. Suggestions?

sam (infra): prioritize 2) and 1) in parallel. I can push scale up (spin 2 more nodes) — reprovisioning may take ~5-8m. @pagerduty can we hold escalation? I'll update on progress in 5 min.

pagerduty: acknowledgment received. Escalation paused until 5m. Will escalate to sre-lead if unresolved.

maria (oncall): executing hosted fallback route now:
```
# temp route override
POST /routing/overrides
{
  "tenant": "acme-finance-dedicated",
  "target": "redwood-hosted/model-xf-small",
  "reason": "dedicated pool pressure - temporary fallback",
  "ttl": "15m"
}
```

tenant-ops-bot: override applied for acme-finance-dedicated -> redwood-hosted/model-xf-small. Routing update propagated to edge in ~12s.

jess (cs): ACME acknowledged the fallback, they'd prefer degraded latency over timeouts. Notifying account team.

sam (infra): kicking off capacity scale: `infra-cli scale-pool --pool dedicated-us-west-2-3 --add-nodes 2 --reason "OOM/kv-thrash"`

sam (infra): terraform apply started, cloud provider provisioning in progress. ETA for nodes to join: ~7m.

luis (sre): while nodes spin up, I'll push a temporary request-size limit at the ingress to block >200k tokens to prevent further cache thrash. Applying rule now.

luis (sre): applied limit: requests over 200k tokens -> 413 Payload Too Large (logged). Rule applied at edge and LB in ~20s.

maria (oncall): good. monitoring p95 now.

tenant-ops-bot: cluster events:
- 2025-10-02T14:03:45Z Node g4dn-12-4 joining pool
- 2025-10-02T14:07:12Z Node g4dn-12-5 joining pool

sam (infra): new nodes joined and pods are scheduling. current_replicas=8. GPU mem utilization dropped to 68% on average.

maria (oncall): p95 dropped from 2.8s -> 420ms after fallback + scale. error rate for ACME dropped from 9% -> 0.6%.

jess (cs): ACME confirms reduced timeouts. They're ok with fallback continuing for another 10m while we stabilize.

maria (oncall): PagerDuty: marking incident as acknowledged and under mitigation. I'll keep thread open for handoff.

sam (infra): root cause notes so far: sudden spike of very large sequences from ACME causing KV cache eviction and GPU OOM pressure. Need follow-ups: - persistent caps on request size for dedicated tenants - autoscaler buffer policy when GPU mem>85% - better tenant-level backpressure and routing fallback automation.

luis (sre): I captured serving logs and heap traces. Will attach to postmortem. Also adding temporary metric: kv_evictions_per_min for tenant.

pagerduty: if unresolved in 10m escalate to SRE Lead (oncall).

maria (oncall): Handoff plan: I'm taking another meeting in 12m, handing this to @sam for watch. Sam, you own follow-up and the postmortem. I'll annotate timeline and handover notes.

sam (infra): taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 30m and then rotate to next oncall if stable. Postmortem owner: sam (infra).

jess (cs): I'll follow up with account team and schedule a technical call with ACME tomorrow to agree on request profiles and limits.

maria (oncall): final notes before I leave: mitigation steps taken: fallback routing applied, scaled pool +2 nodes, ingress token-size limit applied. Impact: partial degraded quality for ACME for ~12m, 0.6% errors post-mitigation. Next steps: detailed RCA, metric dashboards for kv_evictions, autoscaler buffer change, tenant-level throttles.

sam (infra): logging follow-ups in GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/incidents/issues/2025 (RCA + action items).

jess (cs): CS ticket created: CS-7892. ACME updated.

maria (oncall): handing off now — @sam, ack received. I'm leaving the channel. :wave:

sam (infra): acknowledged. continuing watch. I'll update when clearing the incident.

incident-bot: Incident PD#45678 still active. Current status: in mitigation.

luis (sre): captured required artifacts for postmortem. assigning myself to help with RCA.

sam (infra): closing notes later in thread once we confirm stability for 1h. postmortem owner: sam.

jess (cs): thanks team.

-- end of thread --
